what_worked: Strong thesis arc from crowded-AI to narrow-B2B-buyer, with caveats slide and methodology appendix.
fix_next: Recompute all category medians and MRR-per-builder figures against the raw dataset; at least 9 values are materially wrong.
verdict: Compelling narrative undermined by systematically wrong median and per-builder figures.
factual_error_detail: Slide 6/21: AI median $446 vs ref $503; SaaS $303 vs $200.50; Marketing $1,586 vs $2,369.50; Dev Tools $185 vs $635; Health & Fitness $392 vs $662.50; Analytics $1,294 vs $419; E-comm $155 vs $387. Slide 14/21: AI MRR/builder $9,167 vs ~$11,963; Marketing MRR/builder $10,583 vs ~$31,364.

evidence.insight: B2B vs B2C AI split (slide 10) and zero-revenue failure rate comparison (slide 11) are genuinely decision-useful. Top-earner table (slide 12) grounds the thesis in specifics.
evidence.narrative: Clean three-act structure (crowded→wrong target→real yield) with punchy thesis on slide 17 and actionable playbook on slide 18. Slightly diluted by 4 section-divider slides out of 24.
evidence.framing: Slide 2 sets up three questions for founders. Slide 19 handles caveats including small-n and snapshot limitations. Audience is clear throughout.
evidence.accuracy: At least 7 category medians are materially wrong (some by 3x, e.g. Analytics $1,294 vs ref $419). Two MRR/builder calculations are wrong. These errors undermine the core comparative claims.
evidence.visual: Consistent navy/gold palette, clean bar charts with direct labels, good whitespace. Scatter plot (slide 7) lacks numeric axis values. Appendix tables well-formatted.
evidence.ai_slop: none — deck avoids generic filler, every content slide serves the argument

change_reason: Reduced narrative from 8 to 7.5 for 4 divider slides diluting pace; reduced bonus from 2 to 1 given accuracy problems undercut the otherwise strong storytelling.
